properties.title: Who’s afraid of whom in Brussels?
properties.description: Who’s afraid of whom in Brussels? POLITICO’s Halloween guide to who — and what — lurks in EU nightmares. By POLITICO Illustration by Natália Delgado/ POLITICO Night falls in the European capital. Everything’s quiet, but the nightmares are about to begin. Viktor Orbán’s ghost haunts the Schuman roundabout; ash from the bonfire of red tape covers the Justus Lipsius building; Ursula von der Leyen’s chief of staff, Björn Seibert, chases after staffers demanding to know what “associate membership” for Canada actually means; and MEPs tremble at the prospect of construction workers uncovering the skeletons of political intrigues past during renovations. Scared? You should be. Here’s our guide to who is terrified of whom in the Brussels bubble.  Everyone is scared of Marine Le Pen

properties.description: <p>Zelenskyy says ballistic missiles hit crowded areas with no military facilities nearby; truce comes amid reports of growing humanitarian crisis. What we know on day 1,707</p><p><strong>Russian strikes on Kyiv killed one person and wounded eight</strong>, with mayor Vitali Klitschko saying medical facilities and an intensive care unit had been damaged in the late Monday attack. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a ballistic missile attack had struck the grounds of a university campus in the Ukrainian capital. “The missiles hit very crowded areas, and there is not a single military facility nearby. properties.title: Starlink still restricted for Ukraine despite Trump saying Musk lifted speed limits
properties.description: KYIV — Ukrainian interceptors still cannot use the internet at high speed to shoot down Russian attack drones or conduct mid-strike operations as of Friday morning, Ukrainian officials and a drone operator said, despite U.S. President Donald Trump saying SpaceX founder Elon Musk had lifted speed restrictions on his Starshield service. “Morning tests show the speed limits of 140–160 km/h are still there, and the navigation isn’t working properly,” a Ukrainian government official told POLITICO on condition of anonymity. “As of this morning, instances of connectivity loss at speeds of 161 km/h are still being observed.
